text:
maria: Ran a long tail profiling pass on 40B-resnet workload, noticed a sharp KV cache hit cliff around seqlen=512 -> smem kernel switches and ~15% p99 regression. attaching short summary below
kevin: ugh. is cliff deterministic by batch composition or per-device?
aj: deterministic in our runs. small-batch mixed-length (1-512) triggers it. looks like when one request crosses 512 we pick large-tile kernel and it blows register budget for the whole SM
sam: can you paste the perf counters? regs, smem, occupancy?
maria: perfbot run: 
```
SEQLEN=256: regs=32, smem=12KB, occupancy=0.78, kernel=fast-small
SEQLEN=512: regs=48, smem=20KB, occupancy=0.42, kernel=wide-tile
SEQLEN=1024: regs=60, smem=28KB, occupancy=0.26, kernel=fallback-serial
```
kevin: that occupancy drop aligns with register pressure + shared mem per thread. fallback path is more serialized so p99 jumps
aj: interesting part: KV cache hit ratio drops slightly at 512 due to more KV pages being created for larger windows. so both smem/reg and KV churn amplify each other
perfbot: automated-diff: enabling sequence-gating reduced p99 by 8% but increased mean latency by 4% in baseline tests
sam: so naive gating helps but we still have a residual 7% gap. need smarter kernel pick: architecture-aware + per-batch heuristics
maria: proposal: autotuner that uses three signals: estimated regs_needed(seq,batch), kv_cache_pressure(batch_hist), and seqlen_quantile(batch). scorer picks kernel minimizing predicted p99 subject to throughput constraint
kevin: show pseudocode plz
maria: 
```
function pick_kernel(batch):
  est_regs = model_reg_estimate(batch.seqlen_quantiles)
  kv_pressure = kv_pressure_estimate(batch.kv_hotness, batch.size)
  score_small = latency_model('small', est_regs, kv_pressure)
  score_large = latency_model('large', est_regs, kv_pressure)
  if score_small.p99 <= SLO and score_small.mean <= throughput_target: return 'small'
  else if score_large.p99 <= SLO: return 'large'
  else return 'fallback-serial'
```
aj: love it. how do we get training labels for latency_model? historical traces + microbench grid (seqlen x batch x kv-hit)
kevin: microbench plan: sweep seqlen {64,128,256,512,768,1024}, batch {1,2,4,8}, kv_hit {0.2,0.5,0.8}. run on A100 and H100 variant to capture arch differences
sam: include profiling for regs and smem per kernel so tuner can learn constraints, not just latency numbers
maria: rollout plan: 1) offline train models from grid 2) shadow pick with scoring enabled (no routing changes) for 48h collecting labels 3) canary 5% traffic with kill-switch tied to 95th percentile delta 4) full rollout
aj: add metric: frequency of kernel-switch within micro-batch because switching mid-batch kills throughput
kevin: we should also add a quick heuristic rule to avoid picking large kernel when batch contains >10% seqlen > 512 (cheap safety net)
maria: config example for tuner grid: 
```json
{"seqlen_bins":[64,128,256,512,1024],"batch_sizes":[1,2,4,8],"kv_bins":[0.2,0.5,0.8],"arch":["A100","H100"]}
```
perfbot: regression-warn if p99 rises >5% for two consecutive 15m windows
sam: who wants the action items?
aj: I'll own microbench and label collection (runs on perf infra)
kevin: I'll draft the latency_model schema and quick fallback heuristics
maria: I'll wire tuner into kernel-picker and add shadow mode toggle to config
ci-bot: created ticket INF-4122 for microbench, INF-4123 for latency model schema, INF-4124 for tuner integration
kevin: one more thought: consider KV-aware batching where we co-locate high-KV-hit requests to maximize reuse, might reduce pressure a lot
maria: yes but careful with tail latency for single-request flows, maybe optional per-tenant policy
aj: ok let's sync in 30 to align grid and infra slots. thanks folks :thumbsup:
